gloss: from the start; from the very beginning

definitions.gloss: from the start; from the very beginning
definitions.explanation: A set phrase meaning from the beginning of something, often emphasizing that a condition or situation has been true from the outset, or used to indicate starting over from the beginning.

examples.japanese: {最初|さいしょ}からやり{直|なお}す。
examples.english: To start over from the beginning.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は{最初|さいしょ}から{賛成|さんせい}でした。
examples.english: I was in favor of it from the very start.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{最初|さいしょ}からそのつもりだったらしい。
examples.english: It seems he had that intention from the very beginning.

examples.japanese: {間違|まちが}えたので、{最初|さいしょ}から{書|か}き{直|なお}さなければならない。
examples.english: I made a mistake, so I have to rewrite it from the beginning.

notes:
A set phrase combining {最初|さいしょ} (the beginning, first) + から (from). Used to indicate that something has been true since the very beginning, or that an action is being restarted from the beginning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最初|さいしょ}からやり{直|なお}す: to start over from the beginning
- {最初|さいしょ}から{知|し}っていた: to have known from the start
- {最初|さいしょ}から{無理|むり}: impossible from the start
- {最初|さいしょ}からそのつもり: to have intended it from the beginning
- {最初|さいしょ}から{最後|さいご}まで: from beginning to end

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {初|はじ}めから: from the beginning — nearly synonymous; slightly more casual/spoken
- {一|いち}から: from scratch — emphasizes starting over completely, often without relying on any previous work
- {最初|さいしょ}に: at first; initially — indicates a point in time, not a continuous state

USAGE:
Often used emotionally to express that something was obvious or decided early on, as in {最初|さいしょ}からそう{言|い}ってよ ("You should have said that from the start!"). When paired with verbs like やり{直|なお}す, it means to redo from scratch.
